I reported F-DG1-129 in round 8 and verify it as its originating reviewer. I verify F-DG1-213 (qa-verifier) and F-DG1-010 as a qualified non-author, as the assignment directs. At start the real-repo HEAD was 07f1a54, one commit past the freeze commit 273d21f, adding only candidate-excluded metadata: the round-9 assignments, the manifest and stages.json. The recomputed ID is 05915c32 at both commits. During my run HEAD advanced to 39cfc4e, the runner's auto-commit of the domain reviewer's round-9 run. That commit changes only reviews/DG1/round-9, runs/ and test-evidence/DG1/domain/round-9, and the ID stays 05915c32 (50-cleanup.log). checks_run.expected: Every route is a violation: process.kill SIGUSR1, process._debugProcess, process.getBuiltinModule('node:vm'), node:inspector, node:net, node:http, node:sqlite, node:test, node:vm, node:worker_threads, process.execve, (process as any).binding('fs')

The 25 extra variants: node:process/module/child_process/v8/wasi/tls/async_hooks; dynamic import('node:vm'); type-only import; export * from node:vm; node:fs/../vm and node:crypto/../vm; NODE:vm; bare fs/vm; process.dlopen/abort/_linkedBinding/mainModule/on; process?.kill; globalThis.process; aliased and destructured process; process['kill']. checks_run.procedure: Adversarial review of SAFE_NODE_BUILTINS and SAFE_PROCESS_MEMBERS: look for any code-loading, exec, native or debug capability reachable through an allowed entry, and cross-check the lists against the module source's actual node: imports and process.* uses
checks_run.command: grep -rnoE "[\"']node:[a-z_/]+[\"']" apps/api/src/modules | sort | uniq -c; grep -rnw process apps/api/src/modules; gcc -shared -fPIC eng.c; node setengine-probe.mjs eng.so; planted module zz-engine.ts using setEngine + moduleViolations('transformations') + runtime call (clone only)
checks_run.environment: real repo (read-only grep); disposable clone @07f1a54; node v22.22.2 / OpenSSL 3.5.5; gcc
checks_run.expected: No allowed entry carries a code-loading, exec, native or debug capability; the lists are the minimal set the module tree uses
checks_run.actual: FOUND a route. node:crypto's setEngine(path) dlopen()s an arbitrary .so, and its constructor printed NATIVE-CONSTRUCTOR-RAN inside the vitest process. A real module file calling it has moduleViolations = 0 (02-setengine-e2e.log). This is new Low finding F-DG1-130. The members of process are all benign (env, exit, argv, once). Minimality: module source imports only crypto(5), path(3), fs(1) and url(1), and uses no process member at all (the only `process` token is a comment in admin/branding.ts:33). D-055's claim that all seven built-ins and all four members are in use is false: new Low finding F-DG1-131. No legitimate module import or member is wrongly denied (no regression).

summary: PASS. The D-055 default-deny fix verifies. All 12 assigned routes and 25 extra variants are now violations. All 11 positive controls are allowed. architecture.test.ts passes 101/101 and the real module tree has 0 violations. F-DG1-129, F-DG1-213 and F-DG1-010 are CLOSED_VERIFIED. The adversarial review of the allow-list found two new Low, non-mandatory issues. F-DG1-130: node:crypto setEngine(path) dlopen()s and runs a native .so and passes the lint, so the header's 'none loads native objects' claim is false. F-DG1-131: D-055's claim that the allow-lists equal real usage is false (module source uses 4 of the 7 built-ins and none of the 4 process members). Every required check passed except two BLOCKED on the environment: AC-1 effect (no registry) and the Node 24 runtime probe (no binary). All 8 requirements are complete with existing evidence. No Critical/High/mandatory finding is open.
